 This Petition And Appeal, Coming On For Orders,
This Day, Krishna Kumar, J., Made The Following:
 Order

This intra-court appeal by Indian Railways is directed against the order dated 18th October, 2022 passed in Writ Petition No.100586 of 2022, whereby the said writ petition preferred by respondent No.1 herein, was allowed by the learned Single Judge.

2. The material on record discloses that the respondent No.1-Writ petitioner preferred the aforesaid writ petition inter alia contending that 15 guntas of land out of total extent of 3.40 acres in Survey No.39/3 of Sulikeri village of Badami Taluk, Bagalkot District, was acquired for the purpose of Kudachi Railway Project and award dated 23rd September, 2013 was passed granting compensation in favour of respondent No.1.
Subsequently, the appellant issued notification dated 16th July, 2010 which contemplated providing of Group-D NC: 2023:KHC-D:10842-DB employment in favour of the land-losers.
Accodingly, appellant i.e. respondent No.1-writ petitioner applied for the said Group- D post by placing reliance upon the aforesaid notification dated 16th July, 2010.

The said request of the respondent No.1 was rejected by the appellants by issuing impugned endorsement at Annexure-K dated 14th October, 2021 on the ground that the said Circular dated 16th July, 2010 was superseded by subsequent Corrigendum dated 13th August, 2010 and letter dated 28th September, 2010, and also that the said Circular dated 16th July, 2010 was withdrawn by subsequent Circular dated 11th November, 2010.

3. Aggrieved by the aforesaid endorsement at Annexure-K dated 14th October, 2021, the respondent No.1-writ petitioner approached this Court in Writ petition No.100586 of 2022, which was allowed by the learned Single Judge, vide impugned order, which is assailed in the present appeal.

4. A perusal of the impugned order would indicate that the learned Single Judge has come to the conclusion the Circular dated 16th July, 2010 was applicable to the parties, whereas the subsequent Circular dated 11th November, 2019, was not NC: 2023:KHC-D:10842-DB applicable to the parties.

sentences.text:
The learned Single Judge proceeded to uphold the claim of the respondent No.1 by holding as under:
"6.
It is undersigned that the proceedings initiated for acquiring the land belonging to the petitioner culminated in passing the award dated 23.09.2013.

The petitioner in terms of notice issued under Section 12(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and also the Circular dated 16.07.2010, submitted the application with the respondent Nos.4 and 5 to provide them appointment in group 'D' post in the Railway Department.
As n the date when the award was passed and also the application was submitted by the petitioner, the circular dated 16.07.2010 was in force.

In the case of T. Vijayalakshmi and Others (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the application for grant of permission for construction of the building is required to be decided in accordance with law applicable on the date of the said permission is granted.

The respondents Nos.4 and 5 were under an obligation to consider the application submitted by the petitioner in the light of the Circular dated 16.07.2010 which was in force and not the Circular dated 11.11.2019, which superseded the earlier Circular.
As per the Circular dated 16.07.2010, the petitioner was entitled for appointment in Group 'D' post in the Railway Department.
7. The petitioner was also issued with the land losers certificate dated 27.05.2014 in terms of the C i r c u l a r d a t e d 1 6 . 0 7 . 2 0 1 0 .

H e n c e , t h e i m p u g n e d c o m m u n i c a t i o n i s s u e d N C :
2023:KHC-D:10842-DB
by the 5th respondent is not sustainable in law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER
The writ petition is allowed.
The impugned communication dated 11.2.2020 issued by the 5th respondent vide Annexure-K is hereby quashed.

The respondent No.5 is hereby directed to consider the application submitted by the petitioner for appointment in Group 'D' post in the railway Department in the light of the Circular dated 16.07.2010 at Annexure- B pass appropriate order in accordance with law within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Order."
5.

As can be seen from the impugned order, the learned Single Judge merely places reliance upon Circular dated 16th July, 2010 without referring to the Corrigendum dated 13th August, 2010; or letter dated 28th September, 2010.

6. Under these circumstances, the impugned order, insofar as it relates to reference to the Circular dated 16th July, 2010 (Annexure-B), is factually incorrect and the appellant would have to be directed to be reconsider the application submitted by the respondent No.1-writ petitioner without NC: 2023:KHC-D:10842-DB reference to Circular dated 11th November, 2019 and in accordance with law.

In other words, the Circular dated 11th November, 2019 would not be applicable to the respondent The Chairman vs Shri Gadigeppa S/O Muttappa Hanamar ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34467691/
4 No.1-writ petitioner who would be governed by Circular dated 16th July, 2010,
Corrigendum dated 13th August, 2010 and Circular dated 28th September, 2010, all of which had come into existence prior to passing of the award and in accordance with law.
7.
